title: Transfer window planning
summary: Compare and review circular or elliptical orbit changes and moon/planet transfers.

blocks.text: While coasting in a bound orbit, choose Transfers in the flight toolbar, or the Transfer window tab in Maneuver. Local maneuvers offers orbit changes, your moons, sibling moons and the parent body. Interplanetary lets you choose a planet or browse its moons; Star comes last. Find any destination searches collapsed groups and shows parent context. Tab enters lists, arrows or Home/End move, and Enter or Space chooses. Browsing and searching names do not change your committed destination or running transfer search.

Choose one final body and enter the desired low altitude in metres above its reference radius. Turn off Circular target for a separate high altitude. Set Maximum mission time in Julian years: this includes waiting, coasts and intermediate stops, up to 100 years. The default interbody planner compares direct approaches with routes parking around intermediate ancestors. An intermediate stop parks in a high orbit just outside (or inside) the neighbouring moon's orbit, clear of every moon's SOI, so the route avoids paying to descend deep into the parent's gravity well and climb out again; low parking is used only when no such orbit fits. Turn off High parking stops to park low near each stop instead. The selected moon always remains the final destination. Disconnected hierarchies and incompatible providers may have no route. All starting, parking and target orbits must clear terrain and stay inside the relevant SOI.

Find transfer windows compares complete sampled routes. Efficient has the lowest total delta-v found; Faster saves at least 10% of wait plus travel while using at most twice Efficient’s delta-v. The search is bounded and does not promise a global optimum. Each interbody result shows the body sequence, parking stops, number of burns, whole-trip wait/travel and total delta-v. Expand Burn estimates & limits for every burn, including intermediate capture and departure. Complete-route results are checked with the selected finite-burn controller, moving SOI handoffs, contact checks and a full safe revolution at every capture. Same-body orbit changes remain labelled impulsive estimates.

Pause flight while searching to preserve departure windows. Best-so-far results can be adopted while sampling continues; Cancel search discards the search. Changing destination, altitudes, mission time, thrust or source orbit invalidates results. Use plan installs an editable inert sequence and leaves the engine off. Auto warp, beside Use plan, adopts the route, resumes paused flight and enables both automatic execution and auto-warp between burns. You can also choose Execute for each burn, fly manually, or enable those options in the burn editor. Actual encounters and capture are reviewed during execution; a missed encounter or unsafe remaining burn stops automation. Saved and imported plans never arm. Changing the vehicle, providers or orbit needs a new review.
